title: Graceful drain + prefill coordination experiments
content:
Context:
We keep seeing tail spikes when a high-urgency stream arrives right after a large batch consumes most of the slot. Hypothesis: uncoordinated prefill + drain behavior causes starvation and unfairness across co-located tenant queues. This note captures small-run experiments testing coordinated prefill + graceful drain knobs to reduce 99.9/99.99 p95-p99 gaps without regressing median latency or throughput efficiency.

Goals:
- Reduce 99.9 and 99.99 latency spikes attributable to drain preemption and slot monopolization.
- Preserve batching efficiency (tokens/sec) within 3% of baseline.
- Avoid priority inversion where low-urgency long requests block high-urgency short ones.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variables:
  - prefill_threshold: fraction of slot reserved before drain begins (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75)
  - drain_grace_ms: extra ms to let inflight microbatches finish before force-evict (0, 5, 15, 50)
  - prefill_hold_policy: {none, sticky, soft-reserve} 
  - fairness_demote_pct: % of new arrivals demoted when slot nearly full (0, 10, 30)
- Workloads:
  - mixed-tenancy synthetic: 70% small chat (avg 20 tokens), 30% long generation (avg 600 tokens)
  - microburst pattern: 500 req/s short spikes for 200ms every 10s
  - steady conversational: steady 400 rps with token-length variance
- Metrics captured:
  - latency quantiles (p50,p90,p95,p99,p99.9,p99.99) per-tenant and cluster-wide
  - tokens/sec, batch utilization (avg batch size, stddev)
  - fairness score: fraction of high-priority requests with latency > baseline high-prio median
  - drop/evict counts and reason codes
  - kernel occupancy heatmaps and microtrace ids for worst tail events

Instrumentation additions for this run:
- Tag microtraces with drain_phase and prefill_epoch to correlate when prefill window was active
- Emit metric prefill_held_tokens and prefill_reserved_slots per slot id
- Add short-lived debug flag that logs per-slot candidate eviction list when drain_grace_ms > 0

Quick summary of runs (high level observations):
- baseline-run (no coordination): p99.9 spikes to 1.6s under microbursts; fairness score 0.64; avg batch size 18
- prefill_threshold=0.25 + drain_grace=15ms + prefill_hold=soft-reserve: p99.9 drops to 0.88s, fairness 0.81, avg batch size 17 (2.8% throughput loss), eviction count decreased by 40%
- prefill_threshold=0.5 + drain_grace=5ms + fairness_demote=10%: p99.9 ~0.95s, but p99.99 improved only marginally; fairness 0.79; saw more sticky long-lived slots causing mild median regression (p50 +5%)
- prefill_threshold=0 + drain_grace=50ms: reduced abrupt evictions but amplified batch size variance; p99.99 worse than baseline for long generation tenants (likely because long requests held slot longer)

Notable microtrace archetypes that produced tails:
1) Drain-start race: large multi-chunk batch starts draining, microburst of high-urgency short reqs arrive; greedy prefill grabs slot then long inflight prevents flush -> observed p99.9 blips. Trace ids: mt-20251103-17a, mt-20251104-03b.
2) Sticky-reserve stall: soft-reserve left >50% reserved tokens but not filled; new high-urgency arrivals demoted; fairness falloff observed. Trace id: mt-20251105-22c.
3) Eviction thrash: aggressive force-evict with drain_grace=0 caused repeated partial kills and requeueing, increasing queuing latency. Trace ids: mt-20251103-21d, mt-20251106-04a.

Hypotheses and interpretations:
- Small non-zero drain_grace (5-20ms) reduces thrash by letting kernels finish coherent microbatches; too large (>=50ms) lets long gens monopolize.
- Low prefill_threshold (0.25) provides a sweet spot: preserves batching gains while leaving headroom for incoming high-urgency requests.
- Soft-reserve works if coupled with a light fairness demote; otherwise it creates long-lived soft-locked slots that hurt median latency for other tenants.
- Fairness_demote needs to be adaptive based on recent slot-fill variance rather than static %.

Practical config candidate for staging (based on tradeoffs):
- prefill_threshold = 0.25
- drain_grace_ms = 15
- prefill_hold_policy = soft-reserve (timeout 200ms)
- fairness_demote_pct = adaptive: start 10% then ramp to 30% if recent high-prio miss-rate > 5%
- logging: enable microtrace tags for drain_phase for 72h after rollout

Follow-up experiments (next 2 weeks):
- Adaptive demote controller: implement simple PID-like controller that adjusts fairness_demote_pct based on 95th high-priority miss-rate. Quick AB test with canary tenants.
- Prefill timeout tuning: test soft-reserve timeouts [50,100,200,400]ms and instrument blocked_time distribution for other tenants.
- Slot handoff optimization: explore opportunistic yield where a long request yields slot for X microseconds if it has filled >K tokens and there are pending high-urgency arrivals. Measure cost of resumed kernel context switching.
- Sim replay: run the same config over production-sampled arrival traces for 72h to validate steady-state behavior and detect regression windows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we safely expose prefill_threshold per-tenant? Risk: tenant-specific abuse to game batching. Need policy guardrails.
- How does this interact with KV-cache warmup for long sequences? Prefilling slots with warm KV may produce outsized efficiency gains that bias policy.
- Are there kernel-level preemption hooks (CUDA stream priorities) we can use instead of user-space evict/requeue? Investigate with infra team.

Immediate action items (owner tags):
- Clara: implement drain_phase microtrace tagging and push debug flag (ETA: 2025-11-07)
- Miguel: prototype adaptive demote controller skeleton in simulator (ETA: 2025-11-12)
- Priya: run 72h production-sampled replay with candidate config and dump p99.9/p99.99 windows (ETA: 2025-11-17)

Appendix (raw observations):
- Example metric snapshot (prefill=0.25, drain_grace=15ms): p50 24ms, p95 78ms, p99 210ms, p99.9 880ms, p99.99 1720ms; batch utilization 0.88; tokens/sec -2.7% vs baseline.
- Observed eviction reason codes: FORCE_DRAIN_PREEMPT (60%), SOFT_TIME_EXPIRED (25%), KERNEL_OOM_FALLBACK (15%)
- Quick grep of logs: "slot=42 prefill_reserved=120 prefill_held=90 drain_phase=start pending_high_prio=7" (reproduced in mt-20251104-03b)

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments reproducible: check-in config changes under "experiments/graceful-drain" folder in repo.
- Add short runbook for oncall: how to revert drain_grace or disable prefill_hold quickly if regression detected.

End of note.
